review.finding: test_retention_trims_to_keep_last and test_apply_retention_handles_missing_file_gracefully each looped the FULL append_iterate_entry transaction 202/203 times (up from 52/53 at the old cap) -- O(n^2) I/O from _apply_retention's full directory rescan on every call.
review.suggestion: Seed the first N-1 fixtures directly on disk (as test_retention_race.py's _seed_at_cap does) and call the real transaction only once or twice.
review.resolution: Added _write_entries_directly() helper; both tests now seed on disk and call append_iterate_entry once (test_retention_trims_to_keep_last) or twice (test_apply_retention_handles_missing_file_gracefully, to set up + trigger the race). File suite runtime dropped 14.72s -> 4.47s; full retention suite 22.41s -> 7.03s.

review.finding: Module docstring said 'three prose mirrors' but the file guards five locations (docstring, inline comment, F5c.md, hooks-and-pipeline.md, guide.md x2).
review.suggestion: Update the docstring to list all five.
review.resolution: Docstring now names all five locations.

review.finding: test_retention_trims_to_keep_last assigned entry['date'] three times in a row, two of them dead code (one via a malformed non-ISO pattern) with a misleading '# kept for sort' comment.
review.resolution: Superseded by the performance fix above -- the whole loop (and its triple date assignment) was replaced by _write_entries_directly(), which computes the date once.

review.finding: test_retention_does_not_prune_during_migration's docstring claims it verifies migrate-fully-then-retain ordering, but only asserted a post-retention count -- indistinguishable from a hypothetical partial-view-during-migration bug landing on the same count.
review.suggestion: Assert the exact survivor run_id set (newest RETENTION-1 legacy entries + the new one), not just the count.
review.resolution: Added an exact-set assertion (expected_legacy_survivors | {new run_id}) alongside the existing count assertion.

review.finding: ADR's Consequences bullet said 'three prose locations' but the ADR's own later Internal Plan Review section documents two more found afterward (five total) -- the summary bullet undercounted the fix's actual scope.
review.suggestion: Update the Consequences bullet to list all five (or reference Internal Plan Review).
review.resolution: Consequences bullet now lists all five locations and cross-references Internal Plan Review for the two that grep initially missed.
